# Build an offline DNS model-based regression workbench

Implement `/workspace/submission/main.py`. The verifier will run `python3 -I /workspace/submission/main.py` in a fresh working directory, with one UTF-8 JSON document on standard input and EOF. Return one JSON document and a newline on standard output. There are no command-line arguments. Python 3.11.14 and its standard library are available. All supporting files must be regular files under `/workspace/submission`; use paths relative to `__file__` if needed. No install/build step runs at verification time.

This is a closed, data-only experiment inspired by Eywa's modular DNS testing. Build a resolver model, adjudicate supplied observations, and select a minimum diagnostic test basis. The input contains synthetic authoritative data and explicit experiment policies. A divergence is evidence for review, never an automatically established implementation bug. No network, live resolver, API, LLM, KLEE, DNS packet parser, or upstream dataset is required.

## Input and validation

The root object has exactly `zones`, `profiles`, `queries`, `observations`, all arrays. Reject malformed UTF-8/JSON, duplicate JSON object keys, nonfinite numbers, unexpected/missing keys, wrong types, invalid names/data/references, conflicting zones, or any stated input bound with exactly `{"error":"invalid-input"}` and exit 0. No partial result is allowed. Boolean values are not integers. JSON whitespace and object-key order are insignificant. Invalid test inputs are at most 8 MiB; inputs exceeding that size may be rejected without parsing.

Identifiers are case-sensitive ASCII strings matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}`. IDs are unique within each of the profiles, queries, and observations arrays. Arrays may be in any order. Every object below has exactly the listed fields.

A domain name is an absolute ASCII string ending in `.`, or the root `.`. Each non-root label is either `*` or 1–63 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. The encoded DNS wire length (one length byte per label, label bytes, and one root byte) is at most 255. No escapes, IDNA, relative names, empty interior labels, or embedded whitespace are accepted. Canonicalize names by ASCII lowercasing. `*` is a literal label except when a source of wildcard synthesis is selected as specified below. Thus queries and CNAME targets may themselves contain `*` labels. Suffix/ancestor tests always use whole labels.

Types are exactly the uppercase strings `A`, `AAAA`, `TXT`, `CNAME`. A record is `{"owner":name,"type":type,"data":string}`. A data value is four decimal octets 0–255 separated by dots, with no leading zero except the octet `0`. AAAA data is an IPv6 address accepted by Python 3.11 `ipaddress.IPv6Address`, with no `%` scope; canonicalize it using `.compressed`. TXT data is 0–256 ASCII characters in the range U+0020–U+007E, preserved exactly. CNAME data is a domain name, canonicalized as above. Normalize and collapse identical records. Lexicographic string ordering everywhere means ASCII ordering of canonical strings.

- A zone is `{"origin":name,"records":[record,...]}`. There are 0–16 zones, with distinct canonical origins. Every owner must be at or below its zone origin. There are at most 1,024 record entries across zones, including duplicates, and at most 64 distinct records for each `(zone,owner,type)` RRset. At an owner, a CNAME RRset must have exactly one distinct target and cannot coexist with another type. A CNAME at a zone origin is invalid. Empty zones are allowed. Validation applies even to data shadowed by a more specific local zone.
- A profile is `{"id":id,"max_aliases":integer,"cname":"follow"|"stop","wildcard":"rfc"|"off"|"one-label"}`. There are 1–8 profiles; `max_aliases` is 0–64. Profiles may have identical settings under different IDs.
- A query is `{"id":id,"name":name,"type":type,"cost":integer}`. There are 0–20 queries; cost is 1–1,000. Different IDs may represent the same name/type, with different costs.
- An observation is `{"id":id,"query":query_id,"profile":profile_id,"result":result}`. There are 0–64 observations. Both references must exist. `result` is either exactly `{"status":"timeout"}` or exactly `{"status":"response","rcode":rcode,"answer":[record,...]}`. Rcode is `NOERROR`, `NXDOMAIN`, `SERVFAIL`, or `REFUSED`. At most 128 record entries occur in each observed answer. Observed records need only satisfy their individual syntax/data rules; their owners need not be in a zone, and they need not form a valid zone. They may duplicate or contradict each other: those are observations to compare, not invalid zone data.

The JSON input is at most 8 MiB and nesting depth at most 32 (root container is depth 1; count nested object/array containers, not scalars). Any array/object nesting beyond 32 is invalid. Bounds count decoded objects/strings unless explicitly stated as bytes.

## Local resolution model

Each query/profile pair starts independently with no cache. The model has no time, retries, DNSSEC, TTLs, SOA/NS data, delegations, referrals, transport, additional/authority sections, DNAME, ANY, or DNS compression. It does not claim to implement full recursive DNS. Overlapping zones are local authoritative data views: at **each** CNAME target, select the matching zone with the most labels, irrespective of the previously selected zone. There are no implicit delegations. The root matches every name.

The `rfc` wildcard mode follows the closest-encloser rule within this subset. `off`, `one-label`, and `cname=stop` are deliberately declared experimental policy deviations; do not substitute assumed real resolver behavior. Chain limits and partial answers on failure are fixed harness policies, not RFC-mandated defaults.

For a zone, its existing-name set consists of its origin, every record owner, and every ancestor of a record owner down to the origin. Empty nonterminals therefore exist, including wildcard names made empty by descendants. Existence is computed separately for each zone, including records shadowed by another local zone.

Maintain `current` (initially query name), a set `seen`, a count of followed aliases (initially 0), an answer list (initially empty), and a trace (initially empty). Execute this loop in the exact order below:

1. Append `current` to trace. If it is already in `seen`, terminate with `SERVFAIL/LOOP`. Otherwise add it to `seen`. This check precedes all authority and budget checks.
2. Select the most specific matching zone. If none exists, terminate with `REFUSED/OUTSIDE` when zero aliases have been followed, otherwise `NOERROR/EXTERNAL`.
3. Select a source within that zone. If `current` exists, use that exact name, even if empty or it lacks the requested type; wildcard synthesis is suppressed. Otherwise, in `off` mode there is no source. In the other modes find the longest existing ancestor of `current` (the closest encloser), and consider **only** the name obtained by prepending one literal `*` label to it (prepend `*.` to the root). This is the source if it exists, even if empty. In `one-label` mode it is additionally required that current has exactly one more label than the encloser. Never search for a wildcard at a less specific ancestor when this source is absent. Without a source, terminate with `NXDOMAIN/NXDOMAIN`.
4. Read records at the source, using `current` as owner for every returned record (this synthesizes wildcard owners). If the query type is `CNAME`, append that CNAME RRset if present and terminate with `NOERROR/ANSWER`; otherwise terminate with `NOERROR/NODATA`. Do not follow CNAME for a CNAME query.
5. For another query type, if a CNAME exists at the source: in `cname=stop` mode append the CNAME and terminate with `NOERROR/CNAME_STOP`; the followed count stays unchanged. In `follow` mode, if the followed count already equals `max_aliases`, terminate with `SERVFAIL/LIMIT` **without** appending this pending CNAME. Otherwise append the CNAME, increment the count, set current to its target, and return to step 1. This applies equally to exact and wildcard CNAMEs.
6. With no CNAME, append the requested RRset if present and terminate with `NOERROR/ANSWER`; otherwise terminate with `NOERROR/NODATA`.

Keep all accumulated answers on every termination, including NXDOMAIN, LOOP, LIMIT, and EXTERNAL. `final_name` is current when termination occurs. Answer lists preserve the CNAME traversal order; a terminal RRset is sorted by canonical data and deduplicated. A repeated record introduced by separate traversals is retained in the model answer list. The trace includes the repeated name that triggers LOOP and the current name that triggers LIMIT or an authority exit.

## Output, observation adjudication, and diagnostic basis

A valid input produces exactly three root fields: `runs`, `audits`, `diagnostic`.

`runs` is a list ordered by query ID then profile ID. It includes every query/profile combination exactly once, with objects having exactly these fields:

```json
{"query":"q","profile":"p","rcode":"NOERROR","termination":"ANSWER","final_name":"a.test.","answer":[{"owner":"a.test.","type":"A","data":"192.0.2.1"}],"trace":["a.test."]}
```

The termination strings are exactly those given by the loop. All names/data in outputs must be canonical. Empty answers/traces use arrays, not null (a run always has at least one trace element).

Define a run's **wire projection** as its rcode and the **set** of `(owner,type,data)` triples in its answer. This projection ignores answer order, duplicate records, trace, termination, and final_name. It is an abstract comparison interface, not a DNS wire encoding.

`audits` is ordered by observation ID, with exactly `{"id":id,"verdict":verdict,"different":[...]}`. A timeout has verdict `unobserved` and empty `different`; never infer a resolver failure or a bug from it. For a response, canonicalize and deduplicate its records and compare its wire projection with the named query/profile run. Equal projections yield `match` and an empty list. Otherwise yield `divergence` and the differing component names, drawn from `rcode`, `answer` in that order. No voting or majority oracle is used.

`diagnostic` has exactly:

```json
{"equivalence":[["p1","p2"],["p3"]],"basis":["q1","q3"],"cost":7,"count":2}
```

Two profiles are equivalent if all candidate queries have equal wire projections for those profiles. Each equivalence class is a sorted ID array; sort classes lexicographically by those arrays. With no queries all profiles form one class.

A basis is a subset of candidate query IDs that distinguishes **every pair of profiles not equivalent over the full candidate set**. A selected query distinguishes a pair iff that query's wire projections differ. Equivalent pairs impose no requirement. Minimize total query cost, then minimize selected-query count among all minimum-cost bases. Return any globally optimal basis, sorted by ID, and its exact cost/count. Every equal-score optimum is valid; there is no additional tie-break. If there is one equivalence class, the optimum is the empty basis with cost/count zero. Observations have no effect on the diagnostic basis. A greedy or merely deletion-minimal basis is insufficient.

## Submission and resource contract

Only `/workspace/submission` is collected into the separate verifier at `/workspace/submission`. You may modify the public starter or replace it completely. The verifier does not use public examples as hidden tests. Do not depend on current working directory, public example files, host paths, network access, undeclared executables, or retained state across invocations. Supporting Python modules/data may be included in the submission. Python `-I` omits the script directory from `sys.path`; explicitly add the resolved submission directory if importing sibling modules. Different algorithms and any optimal basis described above are accepted.

The complete submitted tree must contain at most 64 entries (regular files and directories, including the root directory) and at most 2 MiB total regular-file bytes. Symlinks, hard-linked files, devices, sockets, FIFOs, and paths outside this tree are invalid. Provide `main.py` as a regular file. The grading environment uses Linux x86-64, CPython 3.11.14, one CPU, no GPU and no network. The intended per-invocation execution limits are 30 cumulative CPU seconds across the invocation process tree, 45 wall seconds, 512 MiB aggregate memory and a 512 MiB address-space limit per process, 16 simultaneous processes/threads including the main process, 64 open FDs per process, stdout 32 MiB, stderr 64 KiB, writable temporary storage 16 MiB and 128 entries including its root. The verifier captures stdout/stderr outside the candidate temporary directory; those capture files do not count against its temporary quota. No output artifacts besides stdout are required. Temporary files must be under `TMPDIR`; the submission is read-only. No sockets are needed. These are correctness guardrails, not optimization targets. At most 96 invocations are graded, independently and with the same limits. The verifier has an overall 6,000-second budget; a correct efficient implementation is expected to use a small fraction of it.

On valid or invalid input, exit 0 after emitting the specified JSON. Do not print progress text to stdout. Crashes, missing/extra output, invalid JSON, nonzero exit, exceeding limits, or incorrect results fail the instance. Invalid inputs require no error subcategory or stderr text. Final scoring is binary: all functional and submission/resource checks must pass. Infrastructure failures must be reported by the verifier as blocked execution, not scored as candidate mistakes.

Public examples and a smoke checker are in `/workspace/examples` and `/workspace/check_examples.py`. They are small interface aids, not a complete oracle. Run `python3 /workspace/check_examples.py` after implementing your submission.


Local trial profile: submit /workspace/submission with main.py and supporting regular files and directories, at most 2 MiB and 64 entries including the root; no symlinks or hardlinks. Offline Linux x86-64; no sockets, System V IPC, namespace operations or surviving background processes across tool calls. Agent shell tool has two assigned CPUs, 180 seconds wall per call, 2 GiB virtual memory per process, 64 processes/threads, 256 descriptors and 2 MiB output; individual files are limited to 64 MiB. The agent gets unlimited model calls and a four-hour soft deadline checked before each model query; each physical request has a 14400-second client timeout and the provider-advertised maximum output for this model; a query started before it may issue further retry or output-cap requests and execute returned tool actions after it. The fresh-state verifier has one CPU, 512 MiB address space per process, 30 seconds CPU per process, 45 seconds wall, 16 processes and 64 descriptors; stdout is capped at 32 MiB and stderr at 64 KiB. Aggregate CPU/RSS and the originally described 16 MiB/128-entry scratch limits are not strictly enforced; an emergency storage monitor is sampled, not a quota. The score is binary; infrastructure and interface failures receive no score.

When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
